correctness.rationale: The first appearances of distinct uniform sampled edges form a random permutation equivalent to independent exponential first-ring clocks. An ordered r-tuple of vertex-disjoint proposed size-two components survives until the last vertex is covered precisely when its own matching-edge completion time and complement coverage time both precede the first forbidden edge. Integrating b exp(−bt)(1−exp(−t))^r against inclusion-exclusion complement coverage produces the finite A_r factorial moments. Finite falling-factorial inversion yields p_y. Conditional on r remaining disjoint edges after coverage, 2r(n−r−1) eligible edges eliminate one/two components and the probability of a two-at-once elimination is (r−1)/(n−r−1); the h_r recurrence and E(Q−T)=Σp_yh_y follow. Ordinary inclusion-exclusion gives E T. Independent exact rational stopping-graph enumeration reproduced the full distributions for n=3,4,5,6, including p2(n=4)=1/5 and extra mean 3/10, with no graph-state Markov assumptions in the derivation. All n≥3 proof is the stated independent-clock and inclusion-exclusion argument, not finite extrapolation.
